sources.text: Dr. Jyoti Mayadev Dr. Mayadev's lab focuses on enhancing the cure through scientific discovery of locally advanced cervical cancer through translational science and clinical trials. The Mayadev lab has a passion to understand the mechanisms of therapeutic response and tumor resistance in cervical cancer. Her lab works on investigations of developmental therapeutic interventions, neoadjuvant strategies with chemoradiation, brachytherapy (internal radiation) optimization, and decreasing disparities in cervical cancer. The mission of the Mayadev laboratory is to use our clinical experience with locally advanced cervical cancer to better understand and shed light on complex problems. Questions that drive our research include: “Why do certain patients recur with cancer and why do some experience toxicity from our treatment? How can be increase the cure rate for patients with large tumors or those with lymph node spread?” We then use all of our available scientific tools, technology, innovation, team science, and knowledge to answer these questions. Everything we do focuses on this strategy; we are sincerely dedicated to cervical cancer innovation. The Mayadev Lab is currently funded by a National Cancer Institute R50 and R01, and Curebound Targeted Grant to innovate and pursue the cure for patients with locally advanced cervical cancer Explore the Lab Focused Projects & Grants Clinical Trials Clinical Trial Advisory Space Media Patient & Provider Resources Featured Articles Automated Treatment Planning Framework for Brachytherapy of Cervical Cancer Knowledge-Based Dose Prediction Models to Inform Gynecologic Brachytherapy Needle Supplementation A Knowledge-Based Organ Dose Prediction Tool for Brachytherapy Treatment Planning of Patients with Cervical Cancer Grants Dr. Mayadev is awarded an NCI R50 and R01 funding for clinical trial progression, translational aspects, and HPV ctDNA investigations to better understand and process treatments for locally advanced cervical cancer.

sources.title: Jyoti Mayadev, M.D.
sources.text: Jyoti Mayadev, M.D. Professor & Vice Chair Education B.A. Biology | Case Western Reserve University 2000 M.D. Case Western Reserve University 2004 Residency University of Washington 2009 Clinical Focus Clinical Focus Gynecologic Oncology, Brachytherapy, Breast Cancer Links Mayadev Lab UCSD Profile About Dr. Mayadev Dr. Jyoti Mayadev is a Professor, Vice Chair of Developmental Therapeutics, Section Chief of Gynecologic Oncology, and Co-Leader of the Gynecologic Oncology Disease Team at the Moores NCI-Designated Comprehensive Cancer Center, University of California, San Diego. She also serves as Director of Gynecologic Brachytherapy, overseeing all clinical and translational research aspects of image-guided brachytherapy for gynecologic cancers, and is an active member of the Breast Cancer Disease Team. A nationally recognized leader in gynecologic radiation oncology, Dr. Mayadev bridges clinical expertise and translational research to advance therapeutic strategies for women with gynecologic malignancies, particularly those with cervical cancer. Dr. Mayadev’s research focuses on the development of national clinical trials in cervical cancer, early-phase therapeutic studies, and novel combinations of immunotherapy with chemoradiation. The Mayadev Laboratory continues to develop innovations that improve outcomes and survival in cervical cancer, and has garnished over $4.5 million in grant funding from the NCI, NRG Oncology, Curebound, Moores Cancer Center, Varian Medical Systems, and Koman for the Cure. Dr. Mayadev currently serves as Co-Chair of the NCI-funded NRG Oncology Cervical Cancer Committee and is the national principal investigator for GOG 9929, NRG GY017, and NRG GY037—phase I and III NCI funded clinical trials investigating immunotherapy with chemoradiation for locally advanced cervical cancer to improve outcomes. Her collaborative R01 grant, Immunogenomic Predictors of Outcomes in Patients with Locally Advanced Cervical Cancer Treated with Immunotherapy and Chemoradiation, builds upon biospecimens from NRG GY017, while her funded NCI R50 grant, NCI Clinical Trial Research Strategy, Harnessing of Equity, and Implementation, aims for innovative science in clinical trials. Dr. Mayadev also served as co-principal investigator of the global phase III CALLA trial, the largest study to date evaluating immunotherapy with radiation in cervical cancer with biospecimens to study ctDNA correlation to response. Before joining UC San Diego in 2017, Dr. Mayadev served as Director of Brachytherapy at UC Davis, where she initiated the image-guided brachytherapy program and led gynecologic and breast oncology research. She completed her radiation oncology residency as Chief Resident at the University of Washington Medical Center and launched her laboratory shortly thereafter. Over her career, she has performed more than 8,000 brachytherapy procedures, published over 200 peer review publications with high impact journals such as Lancet Oncology, Nature Communications, Jama Oncology, Journal of Clinical Oncology, Annals of Oncology, and founded/edited The Handbook of Image Guided Brachytherapy. She has been honored with numerous awards, including the NRG Oncology Outstanding Service Award, ASTRO GYN Chair appointment, Deans Team Award, and Educator of the Year twice.
